abstract: A 43-year-old-man was diagnosed as having primary mediastinal nonseminomatous germ cell tumor based on percutaneous biopsy and an elevated serum concentration of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Although AFP decreased after chemotherapy, the mass size grew and developed tracheal compression by the tumor. The patient was treated with mechanical ventilation and subsequent stent implantation for keeping airway patency. After three cycles of chemotherapy and normalization of AFP, the increased mass was successfully resected and the pathological examination demonstrated a mature teratoma. This case showed a rare clinical manifestation of mediastinal growing teratoma syndrome and successful outcome by multimodal therapies.
abstract_ja: 43歳男性が、経皮生検と血清αフェトプロテイン(AFP)の高値により原発性縦隔非セミノーマ性胚細胞腫瘍と診断された。AFPは化学療法後に低下したが、腫瘤は増大し気管を圧迫した。人工呼吸管理を受け、気道開存維持のためステント留置を行った。化学療法3コース後、AFPが正常化したところで、増大した腫瘤を切除し、病理検査で成熟奇形腫が示された。本症例は、growing teratoma syndromeの稀な臨床像と、多様式治療による良好な転帰を示している。
